paragraphs.text: Yann LeCun, the AI researcher who left Meta at the end of 2025 to found AMI Labs, accused Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei on November 22, 2026 of exaggerating the dangers of AI to get open models banned. LeCun made the remarks in a reply on X to a post about comments Amodei had made at a US congressional hearing, according to OfficeChai and The Open Press.

According to OfficeChai, LeCun wrote that Amodei's message since the GPT-2 era has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal and Amodei would stay in control. He compared the approach to the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic in order to keep control of religious dogma and to stop the population from freely accessing diverse knowledge. He described it as "a new form of medieval obscurantism."

LeCun also linked the argument to Amodei's departure from OpenAI, saying Amodei "left OpenAI because he wasn't going to have control." NewsBytes reported that LeCun suggested this thinking played a part in Amodei leaving OpenAI in 2020 before he co-founded Anthropic.

OfficeChai noted that LeCun has made similar claims before, including accusing Anthropic of publishing questionable studies to scare lawmakers into regulating open models out of existence. NewsBytes summarized his broader view as a warning that restricting access to models slows progress and concentrates power in a few hands.

Amodei has given a different account of why he left OpenAI. The Open Press cited an interview with Bloomberg in which he said that when people do not share the same vision and do not trust each other, there is little point in arguing. He has framed his exit as a question of trust in the direction set by OpenAI's leadership.

On open models, The Open Press reported that Amodei said in July that open-weight models potentially present a higher risk than closed ones because it is very difficult to apply guardrails to them or to monitor how they are used. The outlet added that he has also said Anthropic does not want to ban open models outright. OfficeChai reported that neither Amodei nor Anthropic had responded to LeCun's latest post.

The exchange is the latest round in a long dispute between two camps in the AI industry. LeCun has argued for years that openly released models spread knowledge and keep power from concentrating in a handful of companies. Anthropic sells access to closed models and has been seen as more open to stricter regulation. Because rules on open-weight models could shape which companies can compete, the argument over safety is also an argument over business and influence, and neither side is likely to drop it.
Watch whether Amodei or Anthropic answers LeCun directly, and whether lawmakers who heard Amodei's testimony take up limits on open-weight models.
